nodes.title: The real tower and the existing maximal real subfield
nodes.statement: For m>0, identify F(m)^+=Q(ζ_m+ζ_m^−1) with the existing maximal real subfield. Its elements are exactly the conjugation-fixed elements of F(m). nodes.title: Exact control in a one-prime tower
nodes.statement: Let F∞/F be a Z_p-extension with exactly one finite prime ramified, totally ramified from F, and no other ramification. For every n, Gal(L∞/F_n)≃Y∞⋊Γ_n through a chosen inertia lift, its closed commutator subgroup is ω_nY∞, and restriction induces a canonical isomorphism Cl(F_n){p}≃Y∞/ω_nY∞, where ω_n=γ^(p^n)−1 and Γ_n=Γ^(p^n).
hypotheses: L∞ is the maximal everywhere-unramified abelian pro-p extension of F∞, descended as in I.2. Choice of the inertia section affects the semidirect description but not the final quotient map.
proofSteps: The chosen inertia group maps isomorphically to Γ_n because L∞/F∞ is unramified and F∞/F_n is totally ramified at the unique prime.
Compute commutators of the abelian kernel with the procyclic section; closure is the image ω_nY∞, compact and hence closed.
Kill this inertia group in the maximal abelian quotient to obtain the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_n. Use reciprocity and the intersection F∞∩L_n=F_n.

nodes.title: Eventual ramification and the general inertia kernel
nodes.statement: For any Z_p-extension F∞/F, only finitely many primes ramify, they lie above p, at least one ramifies, and for some m every ramified prime is totally ramified in F∞/F_m. With A_m=Cl(F_m){p}, there is an exact arithmetic sequence ker(Σ_m)→(Y∞)_(Γ_m)→A_m→coker(Σ_m)→0, where Σ_m:⊕_(v ramified in F_m)I_v→Γ_m is the sum of the inertia inclusions. At such m, Σ_m is onto; ker(Σ_m) can have positive Z_p-rank.
hypotheses: All inertia groups and their conjugacy choices are taken in the common maximal extension. No one-prime hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use local tame inertia to rule out infinite ramification outside p in a torsion-free procyclic extension. If no prime ramified, the infinite extension would contradict finiteness of the base class group.
Each nonzero closed inertia subgroup of Γ is open; pass beyond their finite indices. Norm maps A_(n+1)→A_n are then onto by reciprocity and ramification.
Abelianize the maximal unramified extension over F_m and compare the inertia augmentation map with the class group. Keep the kernel map rather than replacing it by a bounded finite error.

nodes.title: The norm relation for the inertia-generated kernel
nodes.statement: For m beyond eventual total ramification, H_m=ker(Y∞→A_m) has finite index in Y∞. If n≥m, H_n=ν_(n,m)H_m with ν_(n,m)=ω_n/ω_m=Σ_(i=0)^(p^(n−m)−1)γ^(ip^m). Consequently #A_n=#A_m·#(H_m/ν_(n,m)H_m). Y∞ and H_m are finitely generated torsion Λ-modules with the same μ and λ.
hypotheses: Use m large enough for surjectivity Y∞→A_m; for application of generic growth increase it beyond the common cyclotomic cutoff.
proofSteps: Choose inertia lifts above each ramified prime mapping to the same γ^(p^m). The kernel H_m is generated by ω_mY∞ and the differences of these lifts and their conjugates.
Raising inertia lifts to p^(n−m) powers gives the norm sum ν_(n,m); this proves equality of the closed generated kernels in both directions.
The inertia-control sequence makes Y∞/(p,T) finite; compact Nakayama gives finite generation. A positive free Λ-rank would make the displayed transition quotients infinite, so Y∞ is torsion.
Use finite index to compare H_m and Y∞; finite kernels and cokernels change eventual cardinalities by a constant, through the imported pseudo-isomorphism calculus.

Apply PM L4’s transition-quotient growth theorem to H_m after the cyclotomic cutoff. It includes finite-error stabilization, vertical counts and horizontal eventual growth; do not replan Appendix A’s generic module lemmas.
Add v_p(#A_m) to the eventual constant and use invariance of μ,λ under finite index and generator change. At p=2 the generic growth step starts deep enough for its automorphism argument.

nodes.title: The bounded p-rank criterion
nodes.statement: For a Z_p-extension of number fields, μ(Y∞)=0 if and only if dim_(F_p)(Cl(F_n){p}/pCl(F_n){p}) is bounded independently of n. Equivalently Y∞ is finitely generated over Z_p. This criterion does not say the p-primary class-group orders are bounded unless λ also vanishes.

proofSteps: Pass to H_m of finite index and use its finite quotient A_m to bound changes in p-rank.
On each vertical elementary summand Λ/(p^a), the p-rank of the transition quotient is deg ν_(n,m), which tends to infinity. On each horizontal summand it is bounded by the polynomial degree.
Finite pseudo-isomorphism errors have bounded p-rank. Thus bounded p-rank is equivalent to absence of vertical factors, and to finite Z_p-generation.

nodes.title: Baker–Brumer logarithmic independence
nodes.statement: Fix embeddings of the algebraic numbers into C_p. If α_1,…,α_r are nonzero algebraic p-adic units and log_p α_i are linearly independent over Q, then those logarithms are linearly independent over the embedded algebraic closure of Q. The conclusion is about algebraic coefficients, not all Q_p coefficients.
hypotheses: Any fixed branch is reduced to the standard unit logarithm; zero logarithms cannot belong to an independent family.
proofSteps: For a finite family choose a common positive integer M, killing the residue and torsion factors and placing every α_i^M in a strict exponential disc; log(α_i^M)=M log(α_i). This works also at p=2 after further powering.

Set ℓ_i=M log_p(α_i). These have algebraic exponentials α_i^M, satisfy the strict radius hypothesis of LinearFormsInLogarithms §8.10, and remain Q-linearly independent. Apply PadicBaker.eq_zero_of_add_sum_mul_eq_zero with constant coefficient zero to each proposed algebraic relation.

Divide by the nonzero rational scalar M to recover the original logarithms. The upstream theorem supplies all auxiliary-polynomial, interpolation and nonvanishing arguments; none is developed again in this roadmap.

nodes.title: Abelian unit character resolvents
nodes.statement: For totally real abelian E/Q of degree d, the rational unit representation (O_E^×/μ(E))⊗Q is the augmentation representation Q[G]/Q·N_G. One can choose a unit α whose d conjugates have only the product relation rationally. For each nontrivial algebraic character χ of G, Σ_(σ∈G)χ(σ)^−1 log_p(σ α) is nonzero.
hypotheses: Embed E into C_p. Deep-unit powering is harmless. The character coefficients are algebraic, even though their logarithms need not be.
proofSteps: Use Mathlib’s logarithmic unit lattice and its full real span. For totally real Galois E, permuting the embeddings makes the logarithmic map G-equivariant into the coordinate-sum-zero hyperplane in R^G; the unit theorem gives an isomorphism after scalar extension to R.

Descend this representation isomorphism to Q as in Sharifi Lemma 1.5.19 and Proposition 1.5.20. Concretely, the equations for equivariant homomorphisms have rational coefficients; a real invertible solution makes their determinant polynomial nonzero, hence it has a rational point with nonzero determinant. The rational augmentation representation is cyclic. Choose its cyclic unit class and clear denominators to obtain an actual integral unit.
Choose d−1 conjugate unit classes independent over Q. Their logarithms are Q-independent because the local log kernel on algebraic units is torsion.
Apply Baker–Brumer; a vanishing nontrivial resolvent would be an algebraic-coefficient relation not proportional to the sole product relation.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of p-adic digit truncations
nodes.statement: Let q=p for p odd and q=4 for p=2; let s_n(x) be the least nonnegative residue of x modulo qp^n. If γ_1,…,γ_r∈Z_p are Q-linearly independent, then for Haar-almost every α∈Z_p the vectors (s_n(αγ_j)/(qp^n))_j are equidistributed in [0,1)^r. For any congruence α≡A mod p^m, d prime to p, target box and sufficiently large n, one can choose α in that congruence with its normalized residues in the box and all s_n(αγ_j) divisible by d.
hypotheses: Use the standard normalized Haar measure and half-open boxes; almost-everywhere is essential. The latter eventual existence follows from a finite torus covering, not from mere infinitude of a visit set.
proofSteps: Apply the imported Weyl criterion. For nonzero t∈Z^r the linear combination c=Σt_jγ_j is nonzero. After a finite initial prefix, the corresponding additive characters on Z_p are orthogonal, so the L² norm of their average is O(1/N).

Apply Chebyshev’s inequality for each positive rational threshold to the squared L² bounds at N=M². Their sum is finite; Mathlib MeasureTheory.ae_eventually_notMem gives almost-everywhere convergence along squares. Fill gaps between squares using |character|=1, and intersect the measure-one sets over countably many thresholds and nonzero t.

For congruence and d constraints, use d invertible in Z_p, scale target boxes, and take a finite covering of the real torus by images of finitely many truncated digit vectors. Shift by powers of p to realize every sufficiently large n.

nodes.statement: For every finite abelian E/Q and every prime p, the class-group invariant μ of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension E∞/E is zero. This theorem is independent of any Iwasawa main conjecture and is available as an input to the Euler-system proof.
hypotheses: The tower is cyclotomic. For p=2 the result is included, with the dyadic normalization and reflection input in G3 explicitly retained.
proofSteps: Apply the arithmetic Bernoulli obstruction, then the same digit-separation contradiction as in the analytic calculation; this uses class-number formulas directly.

Pass from the minus relative class-number exponent to the full arithmetic μ by the Kummer/reflection inequality, after adjoining μ_(2p). At odd p its tame-character form follows from the unramified Kummer pairing and unit exact sequence; the full dyadic version is included in G3.
Descend through finite extensions by class-field norm/transfer control: for E′ containing E, μ(E′)=0 implies μ(E)=0. Do not use a main-conjecture equality in this transfer.

nodes.title: Greenberg’s cyclotomic conjecture
nodes.statement: For a totally real number field E and prime p, Greenberg(E,p) is the conjectural assertion μ(E∞/E)=λ(E∞/E)=0 for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension. Its formal equivalent is that the p-primary orders #Cl(E_n){p} are bounded. For abelian E, Ferrero–Washington reduces this assertion to λ=0 but does not prove it.
hypotheses: The general assertion is recorded as a conjecture; the equivalence is a theorem about the defined invariants.
proofSteps: Apply the general growth theorem with μ,λ nonnegative: bounded orders force both to vanish, and their vanishing makes the eventual order constant.
A finite initial segment does not affect boundedness. Separate the p-primary order from the full class number and the cyclotomic tower from a general Z_p-extension.
